_note: General guidance for PlantVillage classes. Chemical names are examples of commonly recommended active-ingredient groups; always follow the product label and local agriculture officer / KVK advice.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark, velvety spots on leaves and fruit; badly affected leaves turn yellow and drop early.
management: Collect and destroy fallen infected leaves.
Prune to improve air flow through the canopy.
Apply a recommended protective fungicide (e.g. captan or mancozeb group) from green-tip to petal-fall as advised locally.
prevention: Plant scab-resistant varieties where available.
Keep orchard floor clean during winter.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: 'Frog-eye' leaf spots with purple edges and tan centres; rotting fruit and sunken cankers on branches.
management: Prune out dead wood, cankers and dried (mummified) fruit.
Apply a recommended fungicide during the growing season if the disease is common in your area.
prevention: Remove fruit mummies and prunings from the orchard.
Avoid tree stress through proper watering and nutrition.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae); needs juniper/cedar trees to complete its life cycle
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, later with small tubes on the underside.
management: Apply a recommended fungicide from pink-bud to petal-fall stage.
Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts where practical.
prevention: Choose rust-resistant apple varieties.

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery patches on young leaves; leaves may curl and become distorted.
management: Prune to open the canopy and improve air flow.
Apply a sulphur-based or other recommended fungicide at first signs.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser that promotes soft growth.
Remove root suckers and water shoots.

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot_Gray_leaf_sp.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey to tan spots running between leaf veins.
management: If disease is severe before tasseling, apply a recommended fungicide.
Remove or plough in infected crop residue after harvest.
prevention: Grow tolerant hybrids.
Rotate maize with a non-cereal crop.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Small, raised, cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both sides of the leaves.
management: Usually needs no spray on tolerant hybrids; for early, heavy infection apply a recommended fungicide.
prevention: Grow rust-resistant hybrids.
Sow at the recommended time for your region.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (2.5–15 cm), cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on the leaves.
management: Apply a recommended fungicide (e.g. mancozeb group) when lesions first appear, as advised locally.
Destroy infected crop residue.
prevention: Grow resistant hybrids.
Practise crop rotation.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Round tan-brown leaf spots with dark borders; berries shrivel into hard black 'mummies'.
management: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide from bud break to berry set.
prevention: Prune for good air flow and sunlight.
Keep the vineyard free of old infected material.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Complex of wood-infecting fungi (e.g. Phaeomoniella chlamydospora)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow and brown patches between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; vines may suddenly wilt.
management: There is no curative spray. Cut out and burn infected wood well below the damage.
Remove severely affected vines.
prevention: Prune in dry weather and protect large pruning wounds.
Use healthy planting material.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves that later dry out and fall.
management: Remove infected leaves.
Apply a recommended copper or mancozeb-group fungicide as advised locally.
prevention: Improve canopy ventilation.
Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellow mottling on leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green.
management: There is no cure. Remove and destroy confirmed infected trees to protect healthy trees.
Control psyllid insects as advised by your agriculture officer.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery plants.
Monitor regularly for psyllids, especially on new flush.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn purple-brown; centres may fall out leaving 'shot holes'.
management: Apply copper-based sprays as recommended (dormant / early season).
Avoid overhead irrigation.
prevention: Plant tolerant varieties.
Maintain balanced nutrition; avoid excess nitrogen.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown, often with a yellow halo; leaves drop.
management: Remove badly infected plants and leaves.
Apply a recommended copper-based spray.
prevention: Use disease-free or treated seed.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 2–3 years.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-board look), starting on older lower leaves.
management: Remove infected lower leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide (e.g. mancozeb or chlorothalonil group) as advised locally.
prevention: Rotate crops; avoid planting potato/tomato in the same field each year.
Keep plants well nourished — stressed plants are more susceptible.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Pale green, water-soaked patches that quickly turn dark brown/black; white mould on the leaf underside in humid weather. Spreads very fast.
management: Act immediately — remove and destroy infected plants.
Spray a recommended fungicide for late blight (protective, or systemic combinations as advised by your KVK).
Stop overhead irrigation.
prevention: Use certified healthy seed tubers.
Watch forecasts: cool, humid, cloudy weather favours late blight.
Earth up plants to protect tubers.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery spots on leaves and stems that spread to cover the leaf.
management: Remove heavily infected leaves.
Apply a sulphur-based or other recommended fungicide.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties.
Give plants enough spacing and sunlight.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots that join together; the leaf looks burnt or scorched.
management: Remove infected leaves after harvest.
Apply a recommended fungicide if the disease is severe.
prevention: Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering.
Plant healthy runners and renew beds regularly.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit, sometimes with a yellow halo.
management: Remove infected leaves and plants.
Apply a recommended copper-based spray.
prevention: Use disease-free or treated seed and healthy seedlings.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves; leaves yellow around the spots and drop.
management: Remove infected lower leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide (e.g. mancozeb or chlorothalonil group) as advised locally.
prevention: Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves.
Stake plants and rotate crops.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, greasy-looking patches on leaves and stems; white mould under leaves in humid weather; fruit develops brown firm rot.
management: Act immediately — remove and destroy infected plants.
Spray a recommended late-blight fungicide as advised by your KVK.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
prevention: Do not plant tomato near potato fields with blight.
Watch for cool, humid weather and inspect daily.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath; common in humid polyhouses.
management: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity.
Remove infected leaves; apply a recommended fungicide if needed.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties in polyhouses.
Avoid wetting leaves; water at the base.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark edges and grey-white centres containing tiny black dots; starts on lower leaves.
management: Remove infected lower leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide as advised locally.
prevention: Mulch and avoid overhead watering.
Rotate crops and remove plant debris after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites_Two-spotted_spider.cause: Pest — mite (Tetranychus urticae), not a fungus
Tomato___Spider_mites_Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny yellow-white speckles on leaves, fine webbing underneath; leaves turn bronze and dry. Worse in hot, dry weather.
management: Spray water forcefully on leaf undersides.
Use neem oil or insecticidal soap for light infestations.
For heavy infestation use a recommended miticide (acaricide) — not an ordinary insecticide.
prevention: Avoid water stress and dusty conditions.
Protect natural predators such as predatory mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit; can look like early blight.
management: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
Apply a recommended fungicide if spreading.
prevention: Improve air flow by pruning and staking.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus (ToMV) spread by contact, tools, hands and seed
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf curling or distortion, stunted plants.
management: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected plants.
Wash hands and disinfect tools after handling plants.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and resistant varieties.
Avoid tobacco use while handling plants.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward with yellow edges; plants are stunted and flowers drop.
management: There is no cure. Pull out infected plants early.
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, neem products or recommended insecticides.
prevention: Raise seedlings under insect-proof net.
Grow resistant varieties; remove weeds that host whiteflies.
